reason: The cited evidence (E1) supports that reducing Hf increases strength and that a low-density Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr alloy was designed, but it does not address the HfMoTaTiZr system, the specific intervention of reducing only Hf while keeping Mo, Ta, Ti, Zr constant, or the high-temperature (1000 °C) strength retention. Key premises about phase stability, high-temperature performance, and the effect of the specific compositional change are unsupported.
premises: Reducing Hf content lowers alloy density
Reducing Hf content does not decrease, and may increase, strength
The alloy remains single-phase BCC after Hf reduction
High-temperature strength is maintained up to ~1000 °C after Hf reduction
Keeping Mo, Ta, Ti, Zr proportions constant preserves mechanical robustness
